Method of Attack: Storage of master password in plain text
Encrypting master password but leaving encryption key hard-coded in the app's source code
Leaving user passwords in the phone's shared clipboard space
Vulnerable to data residue attacks (password recovery after uninstallation)
Vulnerable to browser autofill phishing attacks
Leaking user data through built-in browsers
Discoverer: TeamSIK (Security Is Key) from Fraunhofer Institute for Secure Information Technology, Darmstadt, Germany
Impacted Systems: Android devices with at least 500,000 installations per app
